newsitem.title: UK: BA will not become "virtual airline" - paper.
newsitem.headline: BA will not become "virtual airline" - paper.

text.p: The chief executive of British Airways (BA), Robert Ayling, has rejected the idea that the carrier will become a "virtual airline," contracting out all its activities apart from marketing, the Financial Times reported on Monday.
In a New Year message to staff, Ayling said BA would unveil a new corporate identity this year, the newspaper said.

The Financial Times quoted Ayling as describing the concept of a virtual airliner as "nonsense" and that the company's business plan envisaged an airline "which has just as many employees in three years time as it has now."

Industry analysts had speculated that BA could become a virtual airline after Ayling announced in September that the carrier planned to save one billion sterling over three years by considering contracting out activities such as baggage handling and ticket processing.
